_doc: GENERATED by tools/consolidate_resident_evidence.py --build. The owner's ratified ladder applied to every identity AS A PROPOSAL. Nothing here is written to a household file: T-0514 mints and T-0515 regrades from this.

G0.says: Every appearance describes a date after the scene year. 1839/1840 alone is never an 1835 resident — later evidence only.

G1a.says: The 1835 poll list and at least one other independent source.

G1b.says: A contemporary record naming the person in Chicago — the 1833-1835 newspapers, which print the person by name in the town.

G1c.says: CONVERGENCE — two or more independent in-window records from DIFFERENT class families (the town's civic lists · the contemporary press, letter lists included · the parish register). Two bodies that did not copy each other naming one man inside the scene window. A letter list is never promoted on its own by this rung; it only COUNTS TOWARD convergence.

G2b.says: An 1833 or 1834 list (poll, tax, muster) with another source.

G2c.says: The St Cyr register 1833-1835 — a party to a marriage or burial in the parish inside the scene window.

G2d.says: Hubbard or Fergus or Norris naming a person the town already carries, with a trade or an address.

G2e.says: A Chicago post-office letter list of 1833-1835 and nothing stronger. The list names a person whose mail is at Chicago; this tool declines to read that as the ladder's `contemporary record naming the person in Chicago` and grades it down. See the policy doc — it is the one reading put back to the owner.

G3.says: A single appearance and nothing else: documented once, placed by nothing. Carries resident_subtype `projected_resident`.

G4.says: Two or more appearances, none of them of a class a rung above accepts. Carries resident_subtype `projected_resident` until a rung above fires.

G5.says: NO PROPOSAL. The town already carries this person and every appearance this consolidation can see describes a date after the scene year — their card rests on sources outside these seven domains (Andreas, the newspapers' own register). The ladder abstains rather than demote a resident on evidence it has not read; the row is listed as a conflict for the owner.
